question.text: The equation of wave is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>160</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math> are in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>s</mi></math>. The speed of the wave is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

solution.text:
The equation of the wave is 

Y=10-2sin2π(160t-0.5x+π4)

The velocity of a wave is given by v=ωk   ...(i).

A wave equation is given by 

Y=Asinωt-kx+ϕ

Using equation (i),

v=2π×1602π×0.5=320 m s-1

⇒v=320×185

⇒v=1152 km h-1
